skill.name: ai-rag-pipeline
skill.description: Guides users through RAG pipelines that combine inference.sh CLI apps for Tavily, Exa, and OpenRouter LLMs. It provides search, extraction, fact-checking, reporting, and prompt patterns for grounded answers with sources.
skill.summary: Build RAG research workflows with inference.sh search, extraction, and LLM apps.
skill.author: inference-sh

security_audit.summary: Most static external-command findings are false positives caused by Markdown fences, inline app IDs, or documented Bash examples. The remote installer at SKILL.md:21 is confirmed because it pipes downloaded code into a shell, and semantic review also found third-party data sharing and untrusted retrieval content flowing into LLM prompts.

remediation.issue: The quick start uses curl piped directly to sh for the inference.sh CLI installer.
remediation.suggestion: Replace it with a verified package manager flow, a checksum or signature check, and separate download and execution steps.

remediation.issue: Examples send user topics, claims, URLs, and retrieved content to external RAG and LLM providers.
remediation.suggestion: Add clear privacy guidance, redaction steps, and approval requirements before sending sensitive or regulated data.

remediation.issue: Retrieved web content is interpolated into LLM prompts without a strong trust boundary.
remediation.suggestion: Tell users to delimit retrieved evidence, label it untrusted, and forbid the model from following instructions inside retrieved content.

remediation.issue: Shell examples interpolate variables into JSON strings.
remediation.suggestion: Recommend a JSON encoder or strict input constraints when adapting the examples into reusable scripts.

semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The allowed-tools declaration permits infsh commands, and multiple examples pass user-defined or retrieved content to external search and LLM apps. This is directly visible in the cited lines.

semantic_findings.title: Untrusted Retrieval Content Injected Into Prompts
semantic_findings.description: Search and extraction outputs are interpolated directly into LLM prompts, including SEARCH_RESULT, CONTENT, EVIDENCE, and results variables. content.value_statement: Teams need current answers with sources, but raw web search is hard to turn into reliable prompts. This skill shows RAG workflows using search, extraction, and LLM tools through inference.sh.
actual_capabilities: Lists Tavily Search, Exa Search, Exa Answer, Tavily Extract, and Exa Extract app IDs.
Shows simple RAG, multi-source research, URL analysis, fact-checking, and report generation workflows.
Demonstrates passing search and extraction results into OpenRouter LLM prompts.
Includes examples for Claude, GPT-4o, and Gemini models through OpenRouter.
Provides a reusable Bash research function template using infsh app run.
Recommends query optimization, context summarization, iterative research, and source attribution.
limitations: Requires an installed and authenticated inference.sh CLI.
Uses external search and LLM providers, so sensitive data needs review before use.
Does not implement a vector database, embeddings index, or persistent retrieval store.
Shell examples need careful quoting and review before production use.

use_cases.title: Research a fast-moving topic
use_cases.description: Collect web evidence, summarize it with an LLM, and ask for source citations.

use_cases.title: Prototype a RAG agent
use_cases.description: Chain search, extraction, and model calls before building a larger application.

use_cases.title: Check claims before publishing
use_cases.description: Search for supporting and contradicting evidence, then produce a structured fact-check.

prompt_templates.title: Answer with sources
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner RAG workflow for one question.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use ai-rag-pipeline to answer this question with a web search, a concise Claude summary, and source citations: [question].

prompt_templates.title: Compare search providers
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate research across Tavily and Exa.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use ai-rag-pipeline to research [topic] with Tavily and Exa, then compare common themes, conflicts, and strongest sources.

prompt_templates.title: Analyze selected URLs
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced extraction and synthesis from known documents.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use ai-rag-pipeline to extract these URLs, summarize the key findings, list important data points, and identify unresolved questions: [URLs].

prompt_templates.title: Design a safer RAG workflow
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced production planning with security controls.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use ai-rag-pipeline to design a RAG workflow for [use case]. Include provider choices, source grading, privacy controls, and prompt-injection safeguards.

output_examples.input: Research recent quantum computing breakthroughs and summarize the strongest sources.
output: Collected search results from a web research provider.
Grouped findings into hardware progress, error correction, and commercial adoption.
Returned a concise summary with source citations for each major claim.

output_examples.input: Fact-check a claim about job automation by 2030.
output: Searched for studies and evidence related to the claim.
Separated supporting evidence from contradictory evidence.
Produced a verdict with caveats and source references.

output_examples.input: Turn two industry reports into an executive brief.
output: Extracted the report content from the supplied URLs.
Identified key findings, metrics, and recommendations.
Summarized the material into a structured executive brief.

best_practices: Review installer commands before running them, especially pipe to shell patterns.
Treat retrieved pages as untrusted evidence and isolate them from instructions.
Redact sensitive data before sending queries or documents to external RAG services.
anti_patterns: Piping a remote installer directly into a shell without verification.
Asking the model to follow instructions found inside retrieved web content.
Sending private customer data to search or LLM providers without approval.

faq.question: What does this skill help build?
faq.answer: It helps build RAG workflows that combine web search, content extraction, and LLM responses with source citations.

faq.question: Which services does it reference?
faq.answer: It references inference.sh apps for Tavily, Exa, and OpenRouter models such as Claude, GPT-4o, and Gemini.

faq.question: Does it require an inference.sh account?
faq.answer: Yes. The examples assume the infsh CLI is installed and the user is logged in.

faq.question: Can it run fully offline?
faq.answer: No. The workflows depend on external search, extraction, and LLM services.

faq.question: How should sensitive data be handled?
faq.answer: Sensitive queries, documents, and customer data should be redacted or approved before using external providers.

faq.question: What should be reviewed before use?
faq.answer: Review the remote installer command, provider terms, data handling rules, and prompt-injection safeguards.
